old_caption: The video captures a flowing stream surrounded by large rocks and boulders. The water cascades over the rocks, creating white, frothy rapids as it moves swiftly downstream. The rocks vary in size and shape, some smooth and others jagged, adding texture to the landscape. The water's surface is dynamic, reflecting light and creating ripples and small waves as it flows. The overall scene is natural and unobstructed, with no visible animals or human characters.
original_wisa_caption: The video captures a serene scene of a flowing stream surrounded by large rocks and boulders. The water cascades over the rocks, creating white, frothy rapids as it moves swiftly downstream. The rocks vary in size and shape, some smooth and others jagged, adding texture to the landscape. The water's surface is dynamic, reflecting the light and creating ripples and small waves as it flows. In the background, a larger waterfall can be seen, adding to the natural beauty of the setting. The overall atmosphere is peaceful and tranquil, with the sound of rushing water providing a soothing soundtrack. There are no visible animals or human characters in the video, allowing the viewer to fully immerse themselves in the natural environment. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, focusing on the movement of the water and the surrounding rocks, emphasizing the natural flow and rhythm of the scene.
caption: The video captures a rocky mountain stream from a low, steady viewpoint. Large lichen-flecked granite boulders anchor the left and bottom foreground, while a cluster of rounded rocks lines the right bank and a white waterfall pours in the upper-left background. A pool of aerated water fills the mid- and foreground, its surface continuously churning as foam, bubbles, and ripples form, shift downstream, and dissipate. A thin bare twig protrudes near the center, remaining fixed in place while the turbulent flow rushes around it. The background waterfall's white plume stays broadly steady in shape and position throughout the sequence. The foreground boulders, right-bank rocks, and background elements keep their positions, with no evident camera movement. Lighting and color tone remain consistent. The churning water is already in motion, conveying an ongoing process rather than a discrete beginning or completion.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
